title: Button to open default gateway in browser
line: In the Networks widget's Details tab, the default gateway is now a link that opens the router's page in the browser.
explanation: The Networks widget's Details tab listed the default gateway as plain text, so reaching the router's web page meant right-clicking, copying the address and pasting it into a browser. The connection details only carried label/value pairs, so the widget had no way to know which value could be opened. Each detail can now carry an optional URL (exposed by ConnectionDetailsModel as detailUrl); the IPv4 and IPv6 default gateways get http://<gateway>, except link-local addresses, which browsers can't open. The widget shows such values in the link color with a pointing-hand cursor and opens them on left click; right-click Copy is unchanged.

commits.message:
applet: open the default gateway in the browser when clicking it

The default gateway in the connection details was plain text, so
opening the router's page meant copying it into a browser. Details can
now carry a link, and the gateway is shown as one that opens it.

BUG: 468990

media.caption: Master: the default gateway is plain text like every other detail.
With the fix: the default gateway is shown as a link.
Master: clicking the gateway does nothing.
With the fix: clicking the gateway opens the default browser (Chrome, here on its first-run screen) at http://192.168.1.1.
